column1: # Internship Watch: top 100 tech companies worldwide by market value.
# Format: one header row
#   rank
# - rank: 1 (largest) to 100
# - name: company name as Henry knows it. Matched against seed/companies.json
#   and existing dashboard companies by a normalized form (lowercase
#   "inc"
#   "global tech"
#   "(Google)" removed)
# - market_cap_usd_billions: number
# - hq_country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the company's headquarters.
# - as_of_date: ISO date the snapshot represents.
# - source: short label for where the number came from.
# - careers_url: optional. When the company's careers page is on a known
#   feed (Greenhouse
#   Amazon.jobs)
column2: scripts/seed.py and job/ranking.py run it through

column1: #   job/feeds/detect.py the same way the "Add company" dashboard form does
#   and store the resulting feed_type/feed_id so the daily job can read
#   postings with no Claude involved. Blank for companies whose feed isn't
#   known yet -- see issue #13: don't guess a board slug here
#   one silently reads someone else's postings instead of failing loudly.
#   Filling these in (from a real
column2: confirmed careers link) is exactly what

column1: #   phase 3's source scout and the "Add company" form's own detection are
#   for.
# This is a manually compiled snapshot (see the pull request description for
# why: no ranking site we found both publishes a clean "top 100 tech
# companies worldwide by market value
# companies" list AND has terms that clearly allow automated/programmatic
# access). Henry (or a future daily-job step) refreshes this file by hand
# each quarter from a public source such as companiesmarketcap.com's
# technology sector list or a financial data provider
# through a pull request like any other change.
# scripts/seed.py loads every row here into the `companies` table with
# status "ranked"
column2: and also stores a copy in `ranking_snapshots` for history.

column1: rank
